title: Restriction of scalars along a finite flat algebra preserves finite projectivity
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $B$ is finite as an $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], finitely presented as an $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and flat as an $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let $M$ be a $B$-module that is finitely presented [def-sc-finitely-presented-module] and projective over $B$ [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Regard $M$ as an $A$-module through $A\to B$. Then $M$ is finitely presented and projective over $A$.

proof.text: *Step 1 (finite presentation over $A$).* $B$ is a finite $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and a finitely presented $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], so $B$ is a finitely presented $A$-module [def-sc-finitely-presented-module] by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-presentation-module-presentation]. Since $M$ is a finitely presented $B$-module, [lem-pc-module-finite-presentation-transitive] applied to $A\to B$ and $M$ shows that $M$ is a finitely presented $A$-module.

*Step 2 (flatness over $A$).* $M$ is projective over $B$ [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], hence flat over $B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat]. As $B$ is flat over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], [lem-pc-module-flat-transitive] shows that $M$ is a flat $A$-module.

*Step 3 (projectivity over $A$).* By Steps 1 and 2, $M$ is a finitely presented flat $A$-module, so it is a projective $A$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-flat-module-projective]. Together with Step 1 this is the claim.
